notes: docs/problems/collatz_lambda_recurrence.md. 'Increasing sequence generated by these rules: a(1)=1, and if x is in a then 2x+1 and 3x+2 are in a.' In the coordinate u = n+1 those rules are u -> 2u and u -> 3u from u = 2, so the sequence is exactly the odd n with n+1 a 3-smooth number, which is Williams's lambda(n) = 1 with her a >= 1. THE LANDING SET OF LAMBDA-RECURRENCE IS THIS SEQUENCE, verified 2026-09-20 in both directions over odd starts below 2e5: all 101 distinct landing values lie in it, and every member of it below the largest landing value is landed on, so it is an identity and not an inclusion. A CHECK THAT FAILED FIRST, worth recording: comparing our landing values against the entry's 60 stored terms reported a mismatch, because the stored data stops around 1.7e4 while landing values reach 1.96e5 -- the membership test was against a truncated prefix, not against the sequence. Generating the set to the needed bound settles it. An earlier comparison also failed for including even n, which the a >= 1 condition excludes.
status: OEIS entry, verified against our landing set
title: Increasing sequence generated by a(1)=1 and the rules x -> 2x+1, x -> 3x+2
